chapter: Early New Orleans drummers and bands
title: Riding the trucks and handing out handbills
summary: He rode trucks handing out handbills while trumpeters like Chris Kelly and Buddy Petit played, but cannot recall their sidemen.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: That was my trumpet player. I used to love to hear him play trumpet. Him and Chris Kelly and Buddy P.T. Those who were trumpet players I used to get on the truck. When they would be playing on the truck I would hop on the truck and ride around. Listen to them. They didn't mind you getting on the truck? They didn't mind me getting on the truck because I used to be so little I could hand the handbills around. Oh yeah. They would get me all full of them. They'd tell me if you're going to ride you'd have to hand the handbills out. And I would hand the handbills out. And I would enjoy listening to them play. And they would stop at every corner. Every corner they'd stop I would hop off the truck and give the bills around. And they would be playing. And they would be playing. And I was like Chinatown, Tiger Rack. Those were his favorites. Yeah. And Muscat Rambo. I used to love them.
Do you remember who was with Buddy P.T. when you'd hear him? Who was in his band? Yeah. The drummer in particular? Who was you?

I don't remember who was in Buddy P.T.T. band. That was a long time ago. But he was playing here at the entertainers. That old club they called entertainers club down on Iberville Street. He was playing there.
But I don't remember who was in his band.
He only had about four or five men in the band at the time. Yeah. And I don't remember who was in his band.
I don't remember Chris Kelly's band. Who might have been with him when you heard him? The drummer or any of the other?
Chris Kelly's band, I think, I don't know who was in his band. That's been pretty long.
